prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1394; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a left-turn collision at an intersection, with the claimant reporting neck pain and whiplash symptoms. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the collision happened as the claimant described, with the claimant's vehicle in the intersection. The other driver gave a matching account, and scene photos are consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 3: Repair estimate on the claimant's vehicle lines up with the force of the impact described, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the inspection. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's effective coverage.

Entry 4: Claimant's medical records show whiplash treatment that followed a usual course, with care tapering as symptoms improved. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is known from prior claims or the medical history provided.

Entry 5: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation, including the recorded statement taken through counsel. The injury reported fits the kind and force of a rear-impact or side-impact collision of this type.

Entry 6: Confirmed that the driver involved is a household member of the policyholder, residing at the same address, and is covered under the policy as such. File is ready for evaluation of the bodily injury claim with counsel's demand pending.
